The Djinn was built from the ground up for Manei Domini troopers, its deliberately slim, almost skeletal frame relying on the operators' cybernetic augmentations to compensate for what unenhanced soldiers would experience as a cramped and unresponsive suit. This design philosophy ran through the entire Demon program: unlike conventional battle armor intended for mass production and general-issue deployment, the Demons were tailored to the cybernetically enhanced elite who would wear them. Whether this was a deliberate engineering choice or evidence of a deeper rift between the Domini and the regular forces commanded by Cameron St. Jamais remained a matter of speculation.

The Djinn became synonymous with Blakist oppression. On Galatea and Gibson, its menacing silhouette became the face of the occupation for civilian populations who rarely saw the larger Celestial OmniMechs up close but learned to fear the battle armor troopers who swept their streets. The suit shared the same unsettling visual aesthetic as its larger Celestial cousins, a deliberate design choice that reinforced the sense of a unified, otherworldly force.

Following the fall of Terra to Devlin Stone's Coalition, a terrorist cell equipped with experimental Djinn prototypes plagued several systems in the former Protectorate. Operating from modified small craft, these insurgents struck at Sirius, New Earth, Liberty, and Altair, deploying modified suits carrying experimental reflective armor in place of the standard model's lighter protection. Local forces eventually began destroying these "Terrorizer" suits, as media outlets dubbed them, and with Blakist supply lines severed, intelligence analysts expected the remaining stocks to dwindle rapidly.

The small laser variant of the Terrorizer trades ammunition dependence for energy-based firepower. A single small laser in the right arm provides indefinite firing capability, limited only by the suit's heat management. Battle claws on both arms enable anti-BattleMech swarming attacks. As with all Terrorizer variants, the suit carries 330 kilograms of reflective armor that halves incoming energy damage, creating a paradoxical resilience against the same weapon type it employs. Jump range remains ninety meters. The laser variant was reportedly the original prototype configuration, with the machine gun and flamer options appearing later as the terrorist cell operating these suits adapted its loadouts to different target profiles. The lack of ammunition logistics makes this variant the most self-sufficient of the three for extended raiding operations.

This Terrorizer variant replaces the flamer with a machine gun in the right arm, providing a marginally longer effective range and better sustained fire capability. Battle claws on both arms retain the suit's ability to conduct swarming attacks. Like all Terrorizer configurations, it mounts 330 kilograms of reflective armor in place of the standard Djinn's lighter advanced plating, dramatically improving survivability against energy-based weapons at the cost of the partial wing and TAG systems. Jump capability is maintained at ninety meters. The machine gun is effective against both unarmored infantry and lightly armored targets, making this the most general-purpose of the three Terrorizer loadouts. Intelligence reports suggest the original prototypes carried small lasers, with the machine gun option emerging as a field modification.

The standard Djinn mounts a single machine gun as its primary weapon, effective against unarmored infantry and capable of suppressing lightly armored targets. Each trooper also carries a light TAG system that can designate targets for homing artillery and missile fire, making even a small formation a threat to heavier units. Battle claws on both arms allow the suit to ride OmniMechs and conduct swarming attacks. A partial wing configuration provides an impressive 120-meter jump range, giving the Djinn exceptional battlefield mobility. The suit carries 200 kilograms of advanced armor, enough to stop a medium laser hit. Its slim profile and light weight make it fast and agile, though its limited direct firepower means the Djinn relies on speed, numbers, and combined-arms coordination rather than individual killing power.

The stealth variant trades the standard Djinn's anti-infantry loadout for a dedicated sniping role. A "David" light Gauss rifle provides precise, long-range firepower, while an electronic camouflage system conceals the trooper from detection until firing. The suit retains the partial wing structure of the standard model, though all flight control systems and avionics have been removed, reducing its jump capability to ninety meters. This deception was deliberate, forcing opponents to guess which Djinn variant they faced until it was too late. The weight savings from removing the wing's active systems allowed for forty additional kilograms of advanced armor, bringing protection to 240 kilograms. The combination of stealth, precision fire, and reasonable mobility makes this variant a patient, methodical killer rather than the terror weapon of the standard configuration.

text.deployment: Four-trooper squads of the electronic warfare variant were embedded within FWLM and Blakist intelligence units. Organized along standard Inner Sphere squad doctrine, these formations conducted deep reconnaissance and signals intelligence missions. The suit's enhanced sensors and ECM package made it valuable for pre-assault intelligence gathering, though the lack of primary armament limited squad-level combat effectiveness.

Five-trooper Points of the electronic warfare variant operated in formations adopting Clan organizational structures. The additional trooper expanded sensor coverage during reconnaissance sweeps and provided redundancy for sustained intelligence-gathering operations. These formations were uncommon, as the variant was produced in limited numbers and primarily assigned to specialized Blakist units rather than general deployment.

Word of Blake Militia Level I formations of six electronic warfare Achileus troopers functioned as dedicated intelligence and electronic warfare elements. Operating within Blakist combined-arms structures, these units provided commanders with enhanced battlefield awareness through their improved sensor suites while disrupting enemy communications and targeting systems. Both SAFE and Blakist ROM employed these formations for covert intelligence operations.

Four-trooper squads armed with the David light Gauss rifle gave FWLM commanders a battle armor formation with genuine anti-armor capability. These squads were assigned to frontline units where they could engage enemy battle armor and light vehicles at range, a significant upgrade from the purely anti-personnel configurations that preceded them.

Five-trooper Points equipped with David light Gauss rifles provided concentrated ranged firepower in formations following Clan organizational doctrine. The additional trooper's contribution to volley fire made the Point a credible threat to light combat vehicles and other battle armor, extending the Achileus beyond its traditional scout role into light strike operations.

Word of Blake Level I formations fielding six David-armed troopers possessed significant ranged striking power. The light Gauss rifle's lethality, multiplied across a six-trooper formation, allowed Blakist commanders to employ these units in ambush roles against enemy reconnaissance forces and light armor, leveraging the suit's stealth to achieve tactical surprise before engaging.

Free Worlds League Military units organized Achileus troopers into standard four-trooper squads, integrating them into existing infantry platoon structures. The flamer-equipped configuration saw frequent assignment to special forces and reconnaissance companies, where squads operated alongside conventional infantry to clear buildings and fortified positions during urban operations. FWLM commanders valued the squad's ability to combine stealth approach with close-range thermal weapons.

Organized into five-trooper Points following Clan formation doctrine, this configuration was fielded by forces that adopted Clan organizational structures. The additional trooper provided greater firepower density per formation, though the Achileus was rarely encountered in Clan-aligned forces given its Inner Sphere origins. Later conflicts saw mixed-doctrine formations employ the suit in this arrangement.

Word of Blake Militia formations organized their Achileus troopers into six-trooper Level I units consistent with ComStar military doctrine. The larger formation size gave Blakist commanders more firepower per tactical element, and flamer-armed Level I units proved effective during the occupation of Terra, where they were employed against resistance forces in urban centers.

FWLM four-trooper squads equipped with the laser configuration served in both frontline reconnaissance companies and rear-area security detachments. The energy weapon's lack of ammunition dependency made it favored for extended patrol missions along the League's borders, where resupply could be difficult. Key governmental facilities and DropPorts were among the installations guarded by laser-armed Achileus squads.

Five-trooper formations using Clan Point organization fielded the laser-armed Achileus in mixed-doctrine operations. The energy weapon's reliability during sustained operations complemented the larger formation's increased scouting coverage. Forces organized along Clan lines found the laser variant's logistical simplicity well-suited to operations where conventional supply chains were disrupted or unavailable.

Word of Blake Level I formations fielding six laser-armed troopers served as dedicated security elements at Blakist installations. The energy weapon loadout eliminated ammunition concerns for static defense assignments, and the suit's stealth capabilities allowed Level I units to establish concealed observation posts around critical facilities, providing early warning against infiltration attempts.

Machine gun-armed four-trooper squads were among the most common Achileus formations in FWLM service. Assigned to general anti-infantry roles within line regiments, these squads provided suppressive fire support during conventional infantry engagements. The configuration's high volume of fire made it effective in the anti-personnel role, though squads required regular ammunition resupply during sustained operations.

Five-trooper Points armed with machine guns offered increased suppressive firepower over standard four-trooper formations. Forces adopting Clan organizational patterns used this configuration for area denial and perimeter defense, where the additional trooper's contribution to sustained fire volume proved significant during prolonged engagements against conventional infantry.

Word of Blake Militia Level I units equipped with machine gun-armed Achileus suits were employed in anti-personnel security operations. Six-trooper formations provided substantial suppressive fire capability, and Blakist commanders deployed these units to secure DropPorts, supply depots, and other logistics facilities where the primary threat came from conventional ground forces rather than armored targets.

FWLM four-trooper squads equipped with target acquisition gear operated as dedicated forward observer teams. Working in coordination with artillery batteries and missile-armed units, these squads used the Achileus stealth profile to infiltrate enemy positions and designate high-value targets for indirect fire. The TAG configuration expanded the FWLM's precision strike capability at the squad level.

Five-trooper Points fielding the TAG configuration provided enhanced target designation coverage through additional formation strength. The extra trooper allowed for continuous observation rotations during extended missions, maintaining persistent target designation capability. Forces organized in Clan Point structure used this configuration to coordinate indirect fire support across wider operational areas.

Word of Blake Level I formations equipped with TAG-armed Achileus suits served as forward observer elements within Blakist combined-arms formations. The six-trooper unit size allowed for split-team operations, with pairs of troopers establishing multiple observation posts while maintaining formation cohesion. Blakist artillery doctrine relied on these units for precision target designation during the Jihad.

Alliance technicians adopted the Salvage Aerie in four-trooper squads for fleet maintenance and recovery operations. These squads worked from Alliance naval stations and mobile repair platforms, supporting both Raven and Alliance vessels. Reports indicated the Alliance began forming independent salvage teams equipped with the suit, though their exact organizational purpose remained unclear to outside observers.

Raven salvage teams organized the Salvage Aerie into five-trooper Points as part of dedicated Salvage Binaries. These Points worked alongside small craft and DropShips to recover damaged vessels, strip battlefield wreckage, and perform emergency repairs across the Clan's scattered fleet. During the Jihad, Salvage Points became critical assets as the Ravens struggled to maintain operational readiness with dwindling resources and no access to homeworld shipyards.

The Salvage configuration saw even more limited distribution than the standard Aerie outside Raven Alliance forces. Any six-trooper formations organized along Level I lines operated in rear-area salvage and recovery roles, supporting fleet logistics where the suit's repair capabilities outweighed its minimal combat utility.

The Outworlds Alliance adopted the Aerie in four-trooper squads consistent with Inner Sphere infantry organization. Alliance marines equipped with the suit served primarily aboard naval vessels, providing boarding defense and security for merchant convoys operating along periphery trade routes. By the mid-3070s, nearly all dedicated Alliance military vessels carried Aerie-equipped marine squads.

Clan Snow Raven deployed the Aerie in standard five-trooper Points, initially with Alpha Galaxy's naval assets. Points typically operated as boarding teams or shipboard security detachments, screening DropShip and WarShip docking bays during fleet actions. As the Raven Alliance consolidated, Aerie Points became a common sight aboard dedicated military vessels patrolling the Deep Periphery and Outworlds Alliance border regions.

Six-trooper Aerie formations organized along ComStar Level I doctrine saw limited circulation beyond the Raven Alliance's primary operators. Small numbers of suits acquired through trade or salvage occasionally appeared in garrison forces along the Alliance border, organized into six-trooper units for shipboard security duties where the suit's space-combat capabilities complemented existing marine doctrine.

Inner Sphere units that salvaged Hell's Horses Afreet variants organized them into four-trooper squads. The one-shot SRM-3 gave even small squads a meaningful opening punch against armored targets, though the rapid expenditure of the missile payload left four-trooper formations reliant on autocannon fire and vibro-claws for sustained fighting.

Clan Hell's Horses deployed the Afreet in standard five-trooper Points, integrating them into combined-arms formations alongside BattleMechs and vehicles per Horse doctrine. The Bearhunter autocannon's devastating close-range output complemented the Horses' preference for aggressive combined-arms assaults, with Points closing rapidly to exploit gaps created by heavier elements.

ComStar or Word of Blake Level I formations equipped with the Hell's Horses variant could deliver a concentrated opening volley of six SRM-3 salvos, a significant first-strike capability against hardened targets. The six-trooper formation offset the one-shot nature of the missile system by massing fire before transitioning to autocannon-based sustained combat.

Inner Sphere forces encountering the Jade Falcon Afreet organized captured suits into four-trooper squads. The fire-resistant armor and AP Gauss Rifle combination proved effective even in smaller formations, though IS commanders struggled to maintain the suits without access to Clan-grade replacement parts.

Clan Jade Falcon Points equipped with the Falcon-specific configuration became a common sight across the Falcon Occupation Zone. Five-trooper Points exploited the AP Gauss Rifle's precision to clear defended positions before heavier Clan assets advanced. Fire-resistant armor proved especially useful during urban operations where defenders frequently employed incendiary weapons.

Word of Blake and ComStar forces that acquired Jade Falcon Afreet suits deployed them in six-trooper Level I formations. The larger formation size amplified anti-personnel capability, with concentrated AP Gauss fire suppressing conventional infantry positions. Level I deployment of the Falcon variant remained rare given the difficulty of capturing intact suits from active Clan garrisons.

Inner Sphere organizations that captured Afreet suits deployed troopers in standard four-member squads. Given the design's Clan origins and limited proliferation outside Hellion, Falcon, and Horse formations, IS-organized Afreet squads were uncommon, typically appearing only among units that salvaged the armor during clashes in the Occupation Zones.

Clan Ice Hellion Points served as the original operators of the Afreet, deploying five-trooper formations in keeping with standard Clan organization. Hellion commanders prized the suit's speed for raiding operations and fast reconnaissance, employing Points as screening elements ahead of heavier Stars. After Clan Jade Falcon captured significant numbers of base-configuration suits, Falcon warriors demonstrated creative field use by loading their recoilless rifles with varied ordnance types, from anti-vehicle rounds to incendiary and flare ammunition.

ComStar and Word of Blake forces organized captured Afreet suits into six-trooper Level I formations. The expanded formation size offset the suit's modest individual firepower, allowing Level I commanders to concentrate recoilless rifle fire more effectively across a wider engagement area.

Taurian search and rescue teams deploy the Ailette Rescue in four-trooper squads, the standard Inner Sphere formation for powered infantry operations. Each squad typically operates from a dedicated SAR DropShip or station, responding to accidents and emergencies across Taurian space.

Clan formations organizing Ailette Rescue operators deploy them in five-trooper Points consistent with standard Clan doctrine. While the suit's Taurian origins limit its availability in Clan space, merchant caste traders and freeborn laborers working in mixed-faction environments have occasionally acquired the design for station-based emergency response.

ComStar and Word of Blake emergency response teams organized Ailette Rescue operators into six-person Level I formations. These units served aboard space stations and orbital facilities where rapid search and rescue capability was essential, with the suit's enhanced mobility proving well suited to navigating cluttered interiors of damaged orbital structures.

Magistracy Armed Forces and Capellan Confederation Armed Forces organize their Amazons into four-trooper squads, consistent with standard Inner Sphere battle armor doctrine. Capellan units frequently integrate Amazon squads into augmented lances alongside BattleMechs and conventional armor, using the suit's ballistic firepower to suppress infantry positions and screen flanks during combined arms operations.

The Amazon's availability through Clan Sea Fox merchant channels has placed small numbers of these suits in the hands of Clan-aligned formations organized along traditional Point structures. Five-trooper Points equipped with the recoilless rifle serve as garrison and second-line assets, where the suit's simplicity and reliability offset its lack of Clan-grade technology.

Republic four-trooper squads equipped with the Recon configuration operated as dedicated sensor teams, typically attached to battalion or regimental intelligence sections. These squads deployed ahead of advancing forces to establish sensor networks along projected enemy movement corridors, feeding real-time data back to field headquarters.

Clan-tradition Points of Recon Angeronas served as the forward eyes of their parent Stars, seeding sensor packages across wide frontages before falling back to covered positions. The five-trooper formation allowed broader sensor dispenser coverage per deployment cycle than smaller IS squads could achieve.

ComStar-tradition Level I formations fielding the Recon variant leveraged their six-trooper strength to establish overlapping sensor grids across larger operational areas. The additional two troopers over a standard IS squad gave these formations enough Remote Sensor Dispensers to cover multiple approach vectors simultaneously.

Republic Armed Forces organized their Angerona troopers into standard four-trooper squads, consistent with Inner Sphere infantry doctrine. The VIII Hastati Sentinels received the first production suits for operational evaluation, with subsequent deliveries reaching other active line formations. Squads typically operated in pairs during scouting missions, providing mutual overwatch while one element advanced through contested terrain.

Clan-influenced formations within the Republic of the Sphere organized Angerona suits into five-trooper Points, following traditional Clan doctrine for battle armor employment. These Points integrated into mixed Stars alongside BattleMechs, riding into combat zones on OmniMech exteriors before dismounting to conduct forward reconnaissance.

Units tracing their organizational heritage to ComStar fielded the Angerona in six-trooper Level I formations. The larger formation size provided additional sensor coverage during scouting operations and allowed the Level I to split into two three-trooper fireteams when terrain or mission requirements demanded independent action.

Captured anti-infantry Asura suits were organized into four-trooper squads by allied forces. The camouflage system and anti-personnel weapons attracted interest for counter-insurgency applications, though the suits' association with Blakist atrocities made their adoption politically sensitive. Most captured examples were studied rather than fielded operationally.

Clan forces showed minimal interest in the anti-infantry Asura variant. Its weapons were optimized for suppressing unarmored personnel, a role Clan warriors considered beneath their combat doctrine. Any salvaged examples organized into five-trooper Points would have been relegated to garrison or second-line duty at best.

Anti-infantry Asura troopers deployed in six-trooper Level I formations during occupation and counter-insurgency operations on Blakist-held worlds. Their camouflage systems and incendiary needlers made them lethal instruments of population control, rooting out resistance cells in urban environments. On Canopus, Asura-equipped Domini troopers of the Forty-first Shadow Division conducted sweeps against local resistance forces with grim efficiency, earning a fearsome reputation among the occupied population.

Inner Sphere forces that recovered Asura battlesuits organized them into four-trooper squads per standard infantry doctrine. The suit's relatively conventional weapons profile made it more accessible to unaugmented troopers than many other Demon designs, though performance reportedly suffered without the cybernetic enhancements the Manei Domini relied upon. Small numbers may have seen post-Jihad service with Republic Armed Forces evaluation units.

Clan encounters with the Asura during the Jihad occasionally produced salvaged examples. Any operational use would have followed five-trooper Point organization. The Asura's comparable mobility to the Elemental and superior weapon range may have attracted some interest, though the suit's lighter armor and Inner Sphere technology base limited its appeal to Clan warriors accustomed to heavier protection.

Standard Asura troopers deployed in six-trooper Level I formations as the Demon series' primary line combatants. Manei Domini Level Is of Asura-equipped troopers engaged enemy battle armor and light combat vehicles at range, exploiting the medium recoilless rifle's reach advantage to damage or destroy targets before closing for rocket-assisted finishing strikes. The suit saw service across multiple theaters, including engagements on New Avalon and garrison duty on Terra during the Blakist occupation.

No confirmed reports document Clan forces fielding SRM-equipped Asura suits in five-trooper Point formations. The variant's close-range ambush role overlapped with capabilities already well served by existing Clan battle armor designs, reducing any incentive to adopt captured examples.

SRM Asura troopers operated in six-trooper Level I formations as ambush specialists within Manei Domini task forces. A full Level I could deliver thirty-six SRM warheads in a coordinated opening volley, enough to cripple a light BattleMech lance or destroy a vehicle platoon. These formations typically operated alongside standard Asura Level Is, with the SRM teams positioned to deliver their payload against targets flushed out by their line-combat counterparts.

Inner Sphere formations that acquired the Black Wolf organized their troopers into four-member squads following conventional infantry doctrine. The suit Clan origins limited initial adoption among Inner Sphere forces, though mercenary commands and allied units operating alongside the Wolf-in-Exile touman occasionally fielded captured or gifted examples. The ER Small Pulse Laser loadout proved popular among these formations for its ammunition independence during extended independent operations.

Clan Wolf and Clan Wolf-in-Exile both deployed the ER Small Pulse Laser configuration in standard five-trooper Points. The energy weapon freedom from resupply concerns made this loadout a favored choice for reconnaissance-in-force missions and extended patrol rotations where logistical support was limited. Points equipped with this configuration often screened for heavier formations, using their sustained firepower to pin opponents for follow-up strikes by OmniMech Stars.

Garrison commands and combined-arms formations occasionally organized Black Wolf troopers into six-member teams to maximize defensive coverage. The ER Small Pulse Laser configuration lack of ammunition dependency made it well-suited to the prolonged defensive operations typical of larger formation deployments, where sustained fire from fixed positions took priority over rapid maneuver.

Inner Sphere units operating the Black Wolf in four-trooper squads found the Heavy Flamer configuration particularly effective in urban security operations. Squads assigned to garrison duty and building clearance missions leveraged the weapon area-denial capability to control chokepoints and deny cover to hostile infantry, compensating for the smaller formation size with the flamer psychological impact on defenders.

During the defense of Knockbridge on Incukalns, Clan Wolf-in-Exile Points armed with heavy flamers sprang a devastating ambush as Jade Falcon forces advanced into the suburbs. The five-trooper formations exploited tight urban corridors to maximize the weapon area effect, turning entire blocks into firetraps that stalled the Falcon assault and bought time for Beta Galaxy withdrawal.

Six-trooper formations fielding the Heavy Flamer configuration were employed primarily in installation defense and area-denial roles. The additional troopers allowed overlapping fields of fire that could seal corridors and access points against infantry assault, making the configuration a natural fit for defending supply depots, command posts, and critical infrastructure against ground-level threats.

Inner Sphere squads equipped with the Heavy Mortar configuration served in fire-support roles, with four-trooper teams providing indirect fire from concealed positions behind friendly lines. The smaller squad size limited the volume of fire compared to larger formations, but allowed the teams to be attached as organic fire support to combined-arms companies without overburdening command structures.

During the invasion of Tharkad in 3143, Clan Wolf Points equipped with heavy mortars obliterated entrenched Commonwealth infantry positions outside the Triad, clearing the way for OmniMech pushes toward the Royal Palace. The five-trooper formation concentrated mortar fire proved devastating against static defenses, with troopers occupying elevated positions in captured skyscrapers to rain indirect fire on defenders below.

Defensive garrisons organized six-trooper mortar teams to provide sustained indirect fire support for fortified positions. The additional troopers increased the formation rate of fire and extended its operational endurance, making the Heavy Mortar configuration a common choice for garrison commands responsible for defending fixed installations against conventional ground assault.

Inner Sphere units fielding the LBX configuration in four-trooper squads employed them as anti-armor hunter-killer teams. The LB-X autocannon cluster munitions gave each squad a credible threat against light vehicles and opposing battle armor, and the smaller formation lower signature allowed these teams to set ambushes along supply routes and patrol corridors.

At Knockbridge on Incukalns, LBX-armed Black Wolf Points of the Second Wolf Legion anchored defensive positions along the Fane River, deliberately drawing Jade Falcon artillery fire away from supporting Cuchulainn suits. When Falcon BattleMechs advanced on their positions, the five-trooper Points exploited the LB-X autocannon cluster ammunition to disable an entire Star of enemy machines, forcing the Falcons to halt their attack and bring up reinforcements.

Six-trooper LBX formations provided area-suppression capability in defensive operations, with the additional troopers delivering heavier volumes of cluster munitions against advancing enemy armor and battle armor. These larger teams were typically assigned to hold critical junctions and crossings where their combined autocannon fire could create overlapping kill zones against approaching targets.

Inner Sphere squads carrying the Plasma configuration operated as specialized anti-vehicle teams. The four-trooper formation allowed rapid deployment alongside mechanized infantry, with the man-portable plasma rifle heat-generating properties making even small squads a meaningful threat to armored targets. Commanders valued the configuration for its ability to degrade enemy vehicle performance through accumulated thermal stress.

Clan Wolf Points armed with plasma rifles played a decisive role during the counterattack at Knockbridge, where their weapons overheated multiple Jade Falcon BattleMechs and forced the surviving enemy units to disengage. The five-trooper formation concentrated plasma fire on individual targets, building thermal loads faster than enemy heat sinks could compensate. This tactic proved especially effective when coordinated with LBX-armed Points that exploited the heat-impaired enemy machines.

Six-trooper plasma formations maximized the configuration heat-stacking potential by concentrating fire from additional troopers onto single targets. Garrison commands employed these larger teams in anti-armor ambush roles, where the combined plasma output of six rifles could cripple even well-protected vehicles before they could withdraw from the engagement zone.

Inner Sphere commanders who obtained hunter-killer Buraqs organized them into four-trooper squads, pairing the Bearhunter-armed suits with conventional reconnaissance assets. The hunter-killer's improved sensors made it particularly valued among IS forces, who lacked comparable scouting platforms at similar speed. Captured hunter-killer suits were prioritized for recovery by Horses salvage teams, making sustained IS operation difficult.

Within a Buraq Star, the single hunter-killer Point provided the formation's primary anti-armor capability. Five troopers armed with Bearhunter superheavy autocannons could cripple light vehicles and threaten exposed BattleMech components in concentrated volleys. During operations aligned with the Mongol Doctrine, hunter-killer Points often led punitive strikes, using their improved sensors to locate hidden defenders before closing to engage.

ComStar doctrine called for organizing captured hunter-killer Buraqs into six-trooper Level I formations when available. The larger unit size concentrated more Bearhunter autocannons into a single command element, increasing the formation's anti-armor capacity. However, the Buraq's Clan-exclusive production and the rarity of hunter-killer variants among salvage made full-strength Level I formations an uncommon occurrence.

Inner Sphere forces that captured Buraq suits organized them into four-trooper squads following standard infantry doctrine. Captured examples remained rare, as Clan Hell's Horses aggressively recovered disabled suits from the field. Those few squads that were assembled typically served in reconnaissance roles, though operators frequently struggled with the quad chassis's unfamiliar movement patterns and the Horses' proprietary communications protocols.

Clan Hell's Horses fielded standard Buraqs in five-trooper Points, the natural organizational unit for the suit's intended role. Ranger Clusters typically assembled full Buraq Stars of five Points, with three Points of the standard configuration providing the formation's scouting backbone. These Points ranged far ahead of heavier elements along the Periphery border, locating pirate camps and tracking bandit movements across the Barrens.

ComStar and Word of Blake forces organized captured or salvaged Buraqs into six-trooper Level I formations. The larger formation size partially offset the suit's limited individual firepower, allowing Level I commanders to establish wider reconnaissance screens. Few confirmed instances of ComStar Buraq deployment exist in the historical record, as the suit's late introduction and Clan Hell's Horses exclusivity limited opportunities for acquisition.

Inner Sphere forces that acquired support Buraqs integrated four-trooper squads into combined-arms formations, valuing the light target acquisition gear above all other features. Even a single squad of support Buraqs could dramatically improve artillery effectiveness for an entire company. IS commanders prioritized these suits for their force multiplication potential, though maintaining the Clan-manufactured TAG equipment proved challenging without access to Horses supply chains.

The support Point within a Buraq Star connected the formation's scouts to rear-area artillery assets. Five troopers equipped with light target acquisition gear could designate multiple targets simultaneously, enabling devastating fire missions against positions identified by the standard and hunter-killer Points. This coordination made the Buraq Star greater than the sum of its parts, turning a light scouting formation into a potent force multiplier for the broader Cluster.

ComStar Level I formations of support Buraqs, when assembled from captured examples, offered significant artillery coordination capability. Six troopers with light TAG equipment could maintain continuous target designation across a wider frontage than the standard Clan Point. The Com Guards recognized the support variant's value and assigned higher recovery priority to these suits than to standard or hunter-killer models.

Inner Sphere factions that have acquired Callistos through Clan Sea Fox trade networks typically organize them into four-trooper squads following standard infantry doctrine. The Bearhunter-armed configuration sees particular favor among garrison commands looking for dedicated anti-infantry capability, with squads deployed alongside conventional forces for base security and urban patrol duties.

Rasalhague Dominion and Wolf Empire formations field Bearhunter-equipped Callistos in standard five-trooper Points integrated within Stars and Clusters. The Bearhunter's anti-infantry capability makes these Points effective as screening elements, clearing enemy foot soldiers ahead of BattleMech advances and securing flanks during offensive operations.

Organizations employing six-trooper Level I formations can field Callistos in this configuration for enhanced anti-infantry saturation. The additional troopers over a standard Clan Point increase the volume of Bearhunter autocannon fire, making the formation effective at suppressing larger infantry concentrations during area denial operations.

Inner Sphere forces operating Callistos in four-trooper squads favor the ER Laser configuration for extended patrol and garrison assignments. The all-energy loadout eliminates ammunition logistics, a practical advantage for commands with limited supply chains. Squads typically operate in support of conventional infantry platoons or light vehicle lances.

Clan Points equipped with the ER Laser configuration excel in extended operations where resupply is uncertain. Dominion and Wolf Empire commanders assign these Points to deep reconnaissance and screening missions, where the energy weapon loadout allows sustained engagement without returning to forward supply points between sorties.

Six-trooper formations using the ER Laser configuration benefit from concentrated energy weapon fire without the logistical burden of ammunition resupply. The formation size suits garrison and security commands that maintain Callistos for continuous readiness, as the energy-only weapons ensure the unit remains combat-capable regardless of supply conditions.

Four-trooper squads armed with the Heavy Machine Gun configuration see regular use in urban clearance operations among Inner Sphere forces. The squad size allows movement through buildings and corridors without crowding, while the weapon's high rate of fire clears rooms and suppresses defenders at close range.

Clan Points carrying the Heavy Machine Gun configuration typically deploy in close terrain where the weapon's rate of fire compensates for its limited range. Dominion garrison forces on contested worlds use these Points for perimeter defense and rapid response to infantry incursions within fortified positions.

The Heavy Machine Gun configuration deployed in six-trooper formations produces a considerable volume of automatic fire. Organizations using Level I-sized battle armor elements assign this configuration to base defense and checkpoint security roles, where the additional troopers ensure continuous suppressive fire during sustained engagements.

Inner Sphere squads equipped with the Medium Recoilless Rifle configuration operate as dedicated fire support elements within combined-arms formations. The four-trooper squad provides accurate ranged fire against light vehicles and fortified positions while maintaining the mobility to reposition alongside conventional infantry advances.

Clan Points armed with the Recoilless Rifle fill a precision fire support role within Stars. Wolf Empire and Rasalhague Dominion commanders attach these Points to BattleMech formations where sustained, accurate fire at range complements the heavier weapons of their parent unit's OmniMechs.

Six-trooper formations with the Medium Recoilless Rifle provide concentrated ranged firepower suitable for defensive operations. The additional troopers allow rotating fire to maintain a steady rate of engagement, making the formation effective at area denial and overwatch assignments along contested perimeters.

text.capabilities:
The SRM 4 variant of Configuration B mounts the heaviest squad support weapon available to the Callisto. An ER Small Laser in the main weapon position provides baseline ranged capability, while the SRM 4 system in the squad support mount delivers a significant salvo of short-range missiles. The Battle Claw on the left arm maintains anti-BattleMech attack capability.

Ground speed compensates for the absence of jump jets on the Elemental-derived frame, and the suit's armor sits below the Elemental standard. The SRM configuration offers the most raw firepower per salvo of any Callisto loadout, making it effective against hardened targets and vehicle formations. The missile system's limited ammunition and minimum effective range are notable drawbacks, requiring troopers to close quickly and make each volley count. Coordinated salvos from a full formation can overwhelm targets that would shrug off individual trooper fire.
text.deployment: Four-trooper squads mounting the SRM 4 configuration serve as close-assault elements against armored targets within Inner Sphere commands. The squad-level salvo can threaten light vehicles and battle armor formations, and coordinated fire from multiple squads provides enough firepower to challenge heavier assets.

Armed Forces of the Federated Suns infantry regiments organized flamer-equipped Cavaliers into standard four-trooper squads, the backbone of Davion battle armor doctrine. These squads deployed extensively during the FedCom Civil War and the Jihad, typically operating alongside BattleMech lances in urban clearance and anti-infantry suppression roles where the flamer's area-denial capability proved most effective.

Clan formations that acquired Cavalier suits through battlefield salvage or Clan Diamond Shark trade organized them into standard five-trooper Points. Clan warriors generally considered the Cavalier inferior to the Elemental, but the suit's availability made it useful for garrison and second-line duties where front-line Clan designs were not allocated. Flamer-armed Points saw use in perimeter defense and anti-infantry screening.

ComStar and Word of Blake forces organized captured and purchased Cavalier suits into six-trooper Level I formations consistent with Com Guard doctrine. Flamer-armed Level I units proved effective during the Jihad, where Word of Blake Militia forces employed them in urban garrison operations and facility defense across occupied worlds.

Laser-equipped Cavalier squads served as the preferred configuration for extended patrol and garrison assignments within the AFFS, where ammunition independence reduced logistical burden. Four-trooper squads with laser armament rotated frequently through border garrison postings along the Capellan and Combine frontiers, providing reliable armored infantry presence without dedicated resupply chains.

Clan Points fielding laser-armed Cavaliers used the configuration's ammunition independence to extend patrol ranges beyond what missile or ballistic-armed formations could sustain. These Points typically served in garrison clusters or as security elements for Clan merchant caste operations, where the suit's IS origin was less of a concern than its operational availability.

ComStar organized laser-armed Cavaliers into six-trooper Level I formations for garrison and security duties. The laser configuration's lack of ammunition requirements aligned well with Com Guard logistical preferences, and these Level I units served in HPG compound defense roles where sustained readiness outweighed raw firepower demands.

Machine gun-armed Cavalier squads filled the anti-infantry suppression role within AFFS combined-arms formations. Four-trooper squads with machine guns deployed alongside BattleMech and armor units to clear conventional infantry positions and secure urban areas during the FedCom Civil War and subsequent conflicts, where their high rate of fire proved decisive against unarmored opponents.

Clan five-trooper Points equipped with machine gun Cavaliers served in rear-area security and anti-infantry roles where Clan Elemental suits were not available. The machine gun's effectiveness against conventional infantry made these Points useful for policing garrison zones and suppressing partisan activity on occupied worlds.

Word of Blake Militia formations organized machine gun-armed Cavaliers into six-trooper Level I units for facility security and population control operations. The machine gun's suppressive capability and the larger Level I formation size provided overwhelming firepower against conventional resistance, a combination the Blakists employed extensively on occupied worlds during the Jihad.

SRM-equipped Cavalier squads served as the AFFS's primary anti-armor battle armor element prior to the introduction of heavier dedicated designs. Four-trooper squads with missile launchers integrated into Regimental Combat Teams across the Federated Suns, providing BattleMech formations with close support capable of threatening light vehicles and exploiting gaps in heavier targets' armor coverage.

Clan Points armed with SRM Cavaliers occasionally appeared in second-line garrison formations where the missile's anti-vehicle capability supplemented heavier Clan assets. These Points typically operated in defensive roles, using the missile launcher's punch to discourage vehicle-borne assaults on fixed positions.

ComStar and Word of Blake Level I formations fielding SRM-armed Cavaliers employed the larger six-trooper unit size to deliver concentrated missile salvos against armored targets. The six-launcher volley from a full Level I could threaten light vehicles and damage BattleMech limbs, giving Com Guard and Militia commanders an organic anti-armor capability within their infantry structure.

AFFS four-trooper squads equipped with flamer Cavalier IIs deployed primarily along the Capellan March, where the suit's stealth armor allowed troopers to close with Amazon-equipped CCAF formations undetected. These squads conducted urban clearance and forward screening operations in border conflicts throughout the Dark Age.

Clan Sea Fox trade networks distributed limited numbers of Cavalier II suits to Clan buyers, who organized them into five-trooper Points. Flamer-armed Points served in garrison roles where the stealth armor's low sensor signature proved useful for perimeter defense and ambush operations.

Organizations that inherited the six-trooper formation standard from the former Com Guard structure acquired small numbers of Cavalier II suits through arms markets and Federated Suns surplus channels. Flamer-armed Level I formations employed the stealth armor to establish concealed defensive positions in urban and forested terrain.

Medium recoilless rifle-armed Cavalier II squads provided AFFS infantry formations with a ranged ballistic option well suited to the open terrain common along the Capellan border. Four-trooper squads used the stealth armor to establish concealed firing positions and engage Capellan battle armor at distances where the original Cavalier's weapons were less effective.

Clan Points fielding the medium recoilless rifle Cavalier II used the configuration's combination of stealth and ranged firepower for reconnaissance-in-force missions. Five-trooper Points leveraged the stealth armor to observe and engage targets from concealment before withdrawing.

Six-trooper formations armed with medium recoilless rifle Cavalier IIs appeared in small numbers among mercenary commands and independent military organizations that adopted the larger formation size. These units used the rifle's range and the stealth armor's concealment to establish ambush positions along defensive perimeters.

text.capabilities: The SRM configuration arms the Cavalier II with a missile launcher in the modular weapon mount, paired with the anti-personnel weapon station for secondary engagements. Clan-specification stealth armor allows the trooper to close within effective missile range without early detection, a significant tactical advantage when delivering a weapon system that demands close proximity to the target. Improved jump jets provide the mobility needed to reach firing positions quickly and withdraw after launching. The missile loadout delivers strong per-salvo impact against vehicles and BattleMech armor, but limited ammunition constrains the trooper to short, decisive engagements. The stealth armor partially offsets this weakness by enabling ambush tactics that maximize the value of each missile fired.
text.deployment: SRM-armed Cavalier II squads gave AFFS infantry commanders a stealth-capable missile platform for anti-armor ambush operations. Four-trooper squads used the Clan stealth armor to approach targets undetected, deliver concentrated missile fire, and withdraw before the enemy could organize a response, a tactic refined during border skirmishes with CCAF forces.

Inner Sphere units that obtained the Volk through trade or salvage organized it into four-trooper squads. The configuration’s emphasis on flanking tactics translated well to Inner Sphere combined-arms doctrine, where squad-sized battle armor elements operated alongside BattleMech lances and conventional infantry platoons in coordinated maneuver operations.

Clan Wolf developed the Volk specifically for its faster flanking units, deploying it in standard five-trooper Points. The configuration found particular favor among Wolf solahma units, freeing dwindling stocks of standard Elemental armor for frontline troops. Though still regarded by some as inferior to the Elemental, Wolf Points employed the Volk’s mobility and melee capability to good effect in screening and harassment operations.

ComStar and Word of Blake forces that acquired the Volk organized it into six-trooper Level I formations. The configuration’s suitability for flanking operations made it a useful complement to heavier Level I battle armor units in Com Guard and Militia combined-arms formations, where six-trooper teams could exploit gaps in enemy defensive lines.

Inner Sphere organizations that acquired the suit through Diamond Shark trade networks or Nova Cat cooperation deployed it in standard four-trooper squads. Draconis Combine infantry units working alongside Nova Cat forces were among the earliest Inner Sphere adopters, integrating the suits into their existing squad-level organizational structure alongside conventional infantry and BattleMech formations.

Nova Cat Elemental Points fielded the Rabid as their primary battle armor throughout the Clan Touman, with five-trooper Points replacing the older Elemental suit in frontline formations. Diamond Shark and other Clan buyers similarly organized their acquired suits into standard Points, maintaining the traditional five-warrior tactical unit structure for integration into Stars and Clusters.

ComStar and Word of Blake formations organized acquired suits into six-trooper Level I units consistent with their military doctrine. The larger formation size provided additional firepower per unit compared to Clan Points or Inner Sphere squads, though procurement remained dependent on Diamond Shark trade channels or battlefield salvage.

Inner Sphere forces aligned with or absorbed from Clan Wolf organized the Rache into four-trooper squads. The enhanced durability suited conventional infantry integration, where sustained firepower and staying power mattered more than the specialized roles of other configurations.

Clan Wolf fielded the Rache in five-trooper Points as an upgraded alternative to older configurations in frontline formations. The enhanced durability gave Wolf Elemental Points greater staying power in direct engagements, allowing them to press attacks that would have forced less protected suits to withdraw.

ComStar and Word of Blake Level I formations fielded the Rache in six-trooper teams. The configuration’s heavier protection made it effective for defensive operations where Level I units needed to hold positions without immediate resupply, and six troopers with improved armor could anchor an infantry position against numerically superior conventional forces.

Inner Sphere security forces equipped four-trooper squads with the light machine gun configuration for direct action missions requiring sustained lethal force. ISF counter-terrorism teams favored this loadout for compound raids, where the machine gun's suppressive fire complemented the grenade launchers' nonlethal options to give squad leaders a full spectrum of escalation choices.

The light machine gun variant was a common choice for Clan police Points tasked with high-threat operations. Five-trooper teams provided enough firepower to overwhelm armed resistance while maintaining the formation cohesion expected of Clan doctrine. Watch strike teams used LMG-equipped Points during operations against Motstånd cells and other armed groups throughout the Dominion.

Six-trooper formations equipped with the light machine gun configuration provided heavy security details for high-value facilities and critical infrastructure. The additional operators allowed LMG-equipped teams to establish layered fields of fire during defensive operations, making this formation and loadout combination effective for static security assignments where overwhelming lethal capability served as both deterrent and response.

Four-trooper squads equipped with the sensor configuration proved effective in Draconis Combine law enforcement, where ISF agents used the improved detection capability to sweep buildings, locate hidden compartments, and track fleeing suspects through urban environments. The smaller squad size allowed sensor teams to operate discreetly during covert investigations.

Clan police forces organized sensor-equipped Constables into five-trooper Points for systematic search operations. Watch reconnaissance teams used the improved sensors to sweep wide areas during counterterrorism operations, detecting concealed weapons caches and locating hidden insurgent positions that conventional search methods could not find.

Draconis Combine agencies organized SRM-equipped Constables into four-trooper squads for operations involving hardened targets. ISF teams used the missile launcher's breaching capability to open fortified positions, with squad members alternating between SRM fire for barrier destruction and grenade launchers for nonlethal crowd management once entry was achieved.

Clan five-trooper Points carrying the SRM configuration served as the primary breaching element in Watch operations against fortified insurgent positions. The Hitomi Compound Siege of 3092 demonstrated both the potential and limitations of this approach, as the single Point's missile armament proved insufficient against a well-defended compound containing over one hundred hostiles.

Six-trooper SRM formations were fielded by organizations requiring anti-vehicle and demolition capability in a law enforcement context. The larger formation offset the single-tube launcher's limited ammunition capacity by distributing engagement responsibility across more operators, allowing sustained fire against barricades, vehicle blockades, and improvised fortifications during extended operations.

Inner Sphere four-trooper squads equipped with target acquisition gear extended the Constable's role beyond direct police action. Draconis Combine agencies paired TAG-equipped squads with supporting military assets during major counter-terrorism operations, allowing precision strikes against identified targets while minimizing collateral damage in populated areas.

Clan military forces that adopted the Constable for secondary roles organized TAG-configured suits into standard five-trooper Points for forward observation and fire coordination. These Points operated alongside conventional military formations, designating targets for artillery and aerospace strikes during operations too large for police forces to handle independently.

Larger six-trooper TAG formations provided enhanced target designation capacity for organizations coordinating with multiple fire support assets simultaneously. The additional operators allowed continuous target marking across wider frontages, making this formation effective during large-scale security operations where rapid, coordinated fire support was required to contain dispersed threats.

The Corona saw limited adoption by Inner Sphere forces, and those who acquired it organized the suits into four-trooper squads consistent with standard infantry doctrine. Integrated alongside conventional mechanized assets, these squads provided ranged fire support that complemented shorter-ranged battle armor formations. The suit's lack of jump capability made it well suited to open terrain operations where sustained firepower outweighed the need for vertical mobility.

Clan Star Adder fielded the Corona in five-trooper Points, the standard Clan organizational unit for battle armor. Corona Points were assigned to front-line formations where they provided ranged fire support to heavier OmniMech Stars. Delivered to the battlefield aboard OmniMechs, a full Point of Coronas could suppress targets at distances that forced opponents to close range or accept attrition, a tactical dynamic Adder commanders refined through sustained operational experience.

ComStar and Word of Blake forces that obtained the Corona organized the suits into six-trooper Level I formations. The larger formation size amplified the suit's ranged firepower, allowing a single Level I to establish effective fire lanes against approaching BattleMech forces. These formations were typically employed in defensive positions where limited mobility was less of a hindrance and sustained output could be brought to bear over extended engagements.

Inner Sphere operators who fielded the SRM configuration organized their troopers into four-trooper squads. The missile-heavy loadout proved attractive for combined-arms operations where close-range striking power was valued over sustained fire at distance. Squads were typically deployed in support of BattleMech lances pushing into contested zones, providing burst firepower during critical moments before falling back on secondary armaments.

Clan Star Adder deployed the SRM configuration in standard five-trooper Points alongside the laser-equipped model. The variant's heavier burst firepower proved effective in close-range engagements, where the opening salvo could disrupt enemy formations before ranged-weapon Points moved in to sustain pressure. Adder commanders learned to pair both Corona configurations in complementary roles, using the missile variant as a shock element and the energy weapon model for sustained attrition.

Word of Blake and ComStar units that acquired the SRM Corona organized it into six-trooper Level I formations. The combined missile output of a full Level I created a significant initial salvo, making the formation a formidable opening strike element in combined-arms engagements. Once ammunition was expended, the formation's backup armaments kept it combat-effective at reduced output compared to the initial engagement.

Lyran Commonwealth units organized Cuchulainns into standard four-trooper squads, integrating them into combined-arms formations alongside conventional infantry and BattleMech lances. The Fourth Royal Guards employed squads to devastating effect during Operation HAMMERFALL on Kosciusko in 3137, where they ambushed retreating Tamarind militia in a road tunnel outside Warsaw. The Twentieth Arcturan Guards deployed a full platoon during the defense of Tharkad in 3143, though the suits' limited mobility proved a liability when Jade Falcon assault BattleMechs pushed through their fire. Wolf's Dragoons also fielded squads during their campaigns along the Federated Suns border.

Clan Wolf-in-Exile organized Cuchulainns into five-trooper Points, the standard Clan formation for armored infantry. The suit was generally available across Exile toumans, and Clan Wolf later acquired additional suits during its 3140 assault on the Commonwealth, distributing them among scattered Elemental Trinaries. A Point of Cuchulainns fought a stubborn rearguard action outside Knockbridge during the defense of Incukalns against the Jade Falcon and Hell's Horses Golden Ordun, buying time for the remaining Wolves-in-Exile to withdraw from the field.

Six-trooper formations of Cuchulainn suits saw limited fielding, primarily among organizations that adopted Level I infantry doctrine. The suit's heavy armor and fire support role made it well-suited to larger formation sizes, though the logistical burden of maintaining six Clan-technology suits per tactical unit restricted adoption to well-supplied commands. Few organizations outside the Lyran Commonwealth's immediate sphere of influence had access to sufficient numbers for six-trooper deployment.

Post-war insurgents operating Terrorizer suits organized in whatever formation sizes their available troopers allowed. Four-trooper cells using the flamer variant struck at civilian population centers on multiple former Protectorate worlds, using the weapon's incendiary capability to maximize terror and property destruction. Local militia forces organized along Inner Sphere lines were the primary responders to these attacks.

No confirmed Clan forces have operated flamer-equipped Terrorizer suits. Five-trooper formations would follow standard Clan Point organization if any captured examples were fielded. The Terrorizer's role as a weapon of terror against civilian targets held no appeal for Clan warriors, and the insurgent cells operating these suits did not encounter Clan garrisons in their documented attacks.

The Blakist terror cell that deployed Terrorizer suits after the fall of Terra organized its troopers into Level I-sized formations of up to six operators, consistent with Word of Blake military doctrine. These six-trooper teams conducted combat drops from modified small craft, striking spaceports and population centers before local forces could mount an effective response. The flamer variant proved particularly devastating in the enclosed spaces of spaceport facilities.

No documented instances exist of laser-equipped Terrorizer suits in Clan five-trooper Point formations. The experimental nature of these post-war insurgent weapons and their geographic concentration in the former Protectorate placed them well outside the reach of Clan salvage operations.

Intelligence analysts believe the original Terrorizer prototypes carried small lasers and were deployed in six-trooper Level I formations during the earliest raids. The energy weapon's independence from ammunition supply chains supported the insurgent cell's need for self-sufficient raiding teams. With former Blakist supply facilities destroyed or captured, the laser variant's logistical simplicity may have been a deliberate design choice rather than a limitation.

Machine gun-equipped Terrorizer cells operating in four-trooper squads were reported on several former Protectorate worlds. The sustained fire capability of the machine gun variant made these squads effective against both security personnel and lightly armored response vehicles. Local police and planetary militia forces, organized along Inner Sphere lines, bore the brunt of these attacks before heavier military units could be mobilized.

No reports document Clan forces operating machine gun-equipped Terrorizer suits in five-trooper Point formations. The insurgent cells responsible for post-war Terrorizer attacks operated exclusively in former Word of Blake territory far from Clan-controlled space, making Clan acquisition of these experimental suits extremely unlikely.

Six-trooper Terrorizer teams armed with machine guns formed the most commonly reported insurgent formation size, suggesting the terror cell retained enough personnel to fill complete Level I units. These teams used their sustained firepower to engage SecurityMechs and responding BattleMechs, with intelligence reports crediting the destruction of at least three BattleMechs across multiple raids on Sirius, New Earth, Liberty, and Altair.

Inner Sphere forces that captured Djinn battlesuits during the Jihad organized them into four-trooper squads consistent with standard infantry doctrine. Most examples ended up with allied intelligence services for analysis rather than front-line deployment, though a handful of intact suits were reportedly fielded by Republic of the Sphere Armed Forces units during the early Republic era. The suits' dependency on cybernetic interfaces made them difficult for unaugmented troopers to operate at full effectiveness.

Clan forces encountered the Djinn during Jihad-era engagements against Word of Blake garrisons and occasionally salvaged intact examples. Any captured suits would have been organized into five-trooper Points per standard Clan formation doctrine. The Djinn's light frame and anti-infantry focus held limited appeal for Clan warriors accustomed to heavier, more directly combative Elemental suits, and no confirmed reports of sustained Clan operational use have surfaced.

The Djinn operated primarily in six-trooper Level I formations within the Word of Blake's Shadow Divisions. Full Level Is of Djinn troopers swept urban areas ahead of heavier Manei Domini forces, using their machine guns and TAG systems to eliminate resistance fighters and designate targets for artillery strikes. On Galatea and Gibson, Djinn Level Is became the most visible symbol of Blakist occupation, their slim, menacing silhouettes appearing in force during pacification operations throughout the Jihad.

Captured stealth Djinn suits proved even rarer than the standard model in allied hands. The few examples recovered intact were organized into four-trooper squads for evaluation purposes. The camouflage system and light Gauss rifle attracted significant interest from intelligence agencies, though the suits' Manei Domini-specific design features limited their practical utility for unaugmented operators.

No confirmed instances of Clan forces fielding captured stealth Djinn suits exist in available records. Any salvaged examples would have been organized into five-trooper Points per Clan doctrine. The stealth variant's sniping role ran counter to most Clan battle armor tactics, which favored direct engagement over concealed fire, further reducing the likelihood of sustained Clan adoption.
